papers.title: Intensive vs Standard Blood Pressure Lowering in People With and Without Chronic Kidney Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
papers.summary: This meta-analysis of 27 trials (88,830 participants) found intensive blood pressure lowering reduced cardiovascular events by 15% per 10 mm Hg lower systolic pressure (RR 0.85), regardless of chronic kidney disease. Kidney failure was not increased, though sustained eGFR declines of 30% or more rose 42%. Absolute benefit was at least as large in CKD.
papers.short_title: intensive blood pressure lowering with and without kidney disease

papers.title: Prevalence of Unrecognized and Recognized Myocardial Infarction in the Rotterdam Study.
papers.summary: No abstract was available for this cohort study, so no results are reported here. According to the journal's one-line summary, it uses Rotterdam Study data to assess temporal trends in the prevalence of recognised and unrecognised myocardial infarction across three epochs. See the full paper for the cohort size and findings.
papers.short_title: recognised and unrecognised heart attacks in the Rotterdam Study

papers.title: Hypertension Management and Control in Cienfuegos, Cuba.
papers.summary: No abstract was available for this population-based cross-sectional survey, so no results are reported here. According to the journal's one-line summary, it assesses hypertension prevalence, management and control in Cienfuegos, Cuba, in 2023, and compares the findings with a similar survey from 2011. See the full paper for details.
